terms.comment: A description of ours, built like Traupman’s tabella tribūtāria for a credit card (see “credit card”), with fidēlitās, faithfulness, as in the Romance names of the thing (carte de fidélité, tarjeta de fidelidad). No reference work has a word for a loyalty card: Traupman, Morgan–Owens, and Levi–Bini were searched.

terms.gloss: a token or ticket that entitles its holder to something: here, a loyalty card
evidence: Suet. Ner. 11: tesserae frūmentāriae, tokens for grain, thrown to the people
terms.comment: Classically a token, a ticket for a distribution of grain or money, or a tally between friends. Its use for a shop’s card is ours.

phrases.english: Have you got a loyalty card?

phrases.latin: Decem crustulīs ēmptīs ūndecimum grātīs datur.
phrases.english: Buy ten biscuits and the eleventh is free.

sources: Lewis & Short: tabella · Lewis & Short: fidelitas · Lewis & Short: tessera
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 213.
